wave_name: Security Hardening (Rate Limiting + Headers + Socket Limits)
goal: Add abuse protection and security headers across HTTP and Socket.io to reduce brute-force and spam risks before feature expansion.

depends_on_outputs_from: ProjectArchitectureSetupAgent: next.config.ts, middleware.ts exists, /lib/env.ts provides NEXTAUTH_URL
AuthenticationAgent: session user.id available for per-user rate limiting context
RealTimeSocketAgent: socket server middleware pipeline available

tasks.title: Implement HTTP rate limiter utility
steps: Create /lib/rate-limit.ts implementing a sliding window rate limiter (Map-based or lru-cache)
Support per-user (session.user.id) keys and per-IP keys
Return a structure that includes allowed:boolean, retryAfterSeconds:number

tasks.title: Enforce rate limiting in middleware.ts
steps: Update middleware.ts to enforce limits on specific routes:
On limit exceeded: return 429 with Retry-After header and JSON { error } shape
verification: Authenticated routes use per-user key, register uses per-IP key

tasks.title: Add HTTP security headers
steps: Content-Security-Policy: baseline restrictive policy compatible with Next.js

tasks.title: Implement Socket.io event rate limiting middleware
steps: Apply per-user event rate limits to abuse-prone events:
On exceeded limit: emit error event to sender, do NOT disconnect socket
verification: Excess events are rejected with error event while socket stays connected

must_provide: How to verify with curl and a socket client
Security header list and expected values

integration_checkpoint.name: Checkpoint D — Security Gate
must_pass: 429 returned correctly for exceeded limits with Retry-After header
Security headers appear on HTTP responses
Socket event rate limiting rejects excess events without disconnecting
commands: socket.io-client script to spam events and verify rejection

stop_condition_to_advance: Security protections are active and verified across HTTP and sockets.
